chapter: Leaving home: Fisk, Tulsa, Arkansas City
title: Tobacco, cigars and chewing tobacco
summary: Stanley's cigarette story leads to McShann's own sickness from chewing tobacco and cigars bought from the grocery store where he worked.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: it's just boom, you know? Yeah. I can remember the very first time I smoked cigarettes. I went home and I went in the back door, felt terrible, but didn't know what was bothering me. Threw up on the kitchen floor and my mother came in, and she could smell it. I don't know what -- what was it in those days you used to get your fingers stained with?
Oh, that was tobacco.
Yeah, I know, but --
Nicotine.
Nicotine.
I know it was the nicotine, but certainly people used to get stains on their fingers much more. But now, they --
Yes, you don't get stains like you did then. And then they used to chew tobacco, you know?
Yes.
They'd chew tobacco, you know, and --
Did you ever try that?

I tried that. See, I used to work at a little old grocery store and every Saturday night, you know, that's my night to have myself a party, you know. I'd work at this grocery store and so Saturday night, I'd goto town. I'd walk to town. But before I'd leave the grocery store, I'd go by and check, 'Let me see. I'll get a little piece of this
tobacco, cut that off, put it in my pocket. Get some candy over here. Look over there and get me a couple of cigars," you know, loading up.
(Laughter.)
I'd go to town, walk all the way to town, a mile and a half, thought nothing of it, walked a mile and a half --
This was at home?
In Muskogee. Smoke my cigar and on the way back from town, chew on tobacco. I'd come in so sick and drunk, I wouldn't know what to do. But I'd come in and go straight to bed.
That chewing tobacco, I mean, that will make you throw up.
Oh, it will kill you. It will. That was the worst I ever had. I left the cigars alone then and I left tobacco alone. That was it. And I let them go.
That chewing tobacco, I mean, once that gets down your throat. I don't know how people manage it.

I never could understand it, because there was a lot of people I used to see and people would come in that store there and after my episode, I couldn't understand how they could handle it. They'd say, "Give me some store tobacco. Give me Brown's Mule." "Give me so on and so on." I'd look at them -- but I don't know, people, I guess their con-
stitution was a lot different.
No, I think there must be some sort of technique to that, chewing tobacco, because you know, probably they don't let it get down their throat.
Well, that could be the thing, because they put it over here or down here or --
They spit when they --
Yeah, everytime you'd look around, that's what they would be doing, you know?
But I could never understand the way they dip snuff, either.
Well, you know --
Did you do that?
I never did try that, because, first of all, I hate to see my grandmother dip snuff. I hated to see her dip snuff and so I hated to see her dip snuff, I just never had the nerve to try it.
